correctness.rationale: For every centrally symmetric admissible six-blocker hexagon, an exhaustive 25-site lattice argument gives first minimum 1, exact short-direction lattice widths give deficit 1/3−min b, and blocker collinearity gives the product equation. Quantitative AM–GM and the identity T²=∏(1−(a−c)²/(1−b)²) yield all barycentric errors O(√ε); corresponding vertices give d_H≤the stated square-root Hausdorff bound when the stated deficit interval. The explicitly given a(t),b(t),c(t) are positive, satisfy the quadratic barycentric identity and are convex with q blockers. Their deficit is quadratic in the deformation parameter, and their support-function excess is linear in the deformation parameter; a rigorous exponent upper limit is proved. Replayed exact-rational script checks 1500 examples, a full auxiliary lattice census, and 201 certified deformation sample brackets; the infinite proof is analytic.

value.rationale: After classification of a unique lattice-transference equality hexagon, quantitative rigidity of near maximizers is mathematically natural. This result gives an explicit uniform metric error bound throughout the whole admissible near-equality six-blocker chamber, demonstrates a genuine quadratic-flat perturbation mechanism, and determines the optimal rate exponent one-half. It is not a mere additional decimal constant or isolated sample; it supplies an exact local stability law and a sharp boundary of possible improvement. Coefficient and global-chamber extensions remain open.
